correctness.rationale: For the real Day--James hexagon N(u,v)=max(|u|,|v|,|u-v|), 0<r<=rho and p=4, separate convexity reduces fixed-scale maximization to 36 ordered vertices. The exact envelope is max(1+(r+t)^4,(1+rt)^4+max(r,t)^4). Independently enumerated all 36 vertex pairs over multiple r,t checks (diagnostic, not continuum proof) and differentiated both scalar branches symbolically. The RESULT.md proof: A_r(t) increases through t=1 for r<=rho; B_{0,r}(t) increases on [0,r] because its derivative E_r>0 using (1+t²)^3(1-t²)>=1 for t<=rho<.84; B_r(t) on [r,1] has exactly one maximum because t³[1-(1+rt)^(-3)] strictly increases. Its t=1 critical derivative is r(r³+2r²-2). Thus t_r in (r,1], (t_r³-r)(1+rt_r)^3=t_r³, and quotient is ((1+rt_r)^4+t_r^4)/(4(1+r^4)(1+t_r^4)). At r=rho t_r=1. Finite sampling does not prove the vertex envelope, but algebraic case checking and continuum convexity do; the analytic derivative argument covers all r.
